subject: Placing random effects vector inside inla.make.lincombs() function

messages.author: 5b5ac0e901ae0add
messages.subject: Placing random effects vector inside inla.make.lincombs() function
parts:
Having trouble estimating a linear combination of effects using the lincombs() function.  Would like to estimate a linear combination of some but not all random effects and fixed effects, but it appears that the only random effect included in all linear combinations is the first.  The lincomb() function appears to work fine, and I can use it as a work-around by concatenating one of these for each required random effect (example below). 
 
This seems to be true even for a simple adaptation of the lincomb() FAQ example:
 
## A simple model
n = 100
a = rnorm(n)
b = rnorm(n)
idx = 1:n
y = rnorm(n) + a + b
formula = y ~ 1 + a + b + f(idx, model="iid")

lc1 = inla.make.lincomb(idx = c(1,NA,rep(NA,n-2))) #estimate random effect for 1st level of idx
lc2 = inla.make.lincomb(idx = c(NA,1,rep(NA,n-2))) #estimate random effect for 2nd level of idx
all.lc = c(lc1,lc2)
names(all.lc) <- c("lc1","lc2")
lc3 = inla.make.lincombs(idx = c(1,1,rep(NA,n-2))) #estimate random effects of 1st & 2nd levels of idx 

r1 = inla(formula, data = data.frame(a,b,y),lincomb = all.lc,control.data = list(initial=10, fixed=TRUE), 
control.inla= list(lincomb.derived.only=TRUE,verbose=T))

r1$summary.lincomb.derived$mean[1] == r1$summary.random$idx$mean[1] #evaluates to TRUE
r1$summary.lincomb.derived$mean[2] == r1$summary.random$idx$mean[2] #evaluates to TRUE 

r2 = inla(formula, data = data.frame(a,b,y),lincomb = lc3,control.data = list(initial=10, fixed=TRUE), 
control.inla = list(lincomb.derived.only=TRUE))

r2$summary.lincomb.derived$mean[1] == r2$summary.random$idx$mean[1] #evaluates to TRUE
r2$summary.lincomb.derived$mean[2] == r2$summary.random$idx$mean[2] #evaluates to FALSE because the left-hand side of the equality just repeats the random effect for the 1st idx level
I'm sure I'm missing some subtlety of the lincombs() specification.  Can you help?  Thanks.

On Sat, 2012-04-14 at 20:46 -0700, David wrote:
> Having trouble estimating a linear combination of effects using the
> lincombs() function. Would like to estimate a linear combination of
> some but not all random effects and fixed effects, but it appears that
> the only random effect included in all linear combinations is the
> first. The lincomb() function appears to work fine, and I can use it
> as a work-around by concatenating one of these for each required
> random effect (example below).

as model 'idx' has length > 1 or a f()-model, then its entry in
make.lincomb is a vector and a matrix in make.lincomb*s*. That is the
error.

the notion is that

inla.make.lincombs(idx = A)

where A is a matrix, is the same as the union of

inla.make.lincomb(idx = A[1,])

and so, for all the rows. so each *row* of A spesify on linear
combination.

I attach an updated and corrected example, hope this helps.
